q: The platoon conducted a reconnaissance mission near the border. “Reconnaissance” means:
e: Reconnaissance = observing an area to collect intelligence (recon).

q: The two sides finally agreed to a ceasefire. A “ceasefire” is:
o: a temporary stop in the fighting
e: Ceasefire = suspension of hostilities.

q: Additional troops were deployed to the region. “Deployed” means:
e: To deploy = to move forces into position.

q: The enemy suffered heavy casualties. “Casualties” are:
e: Casualties = personnel killed, wounded, or missing.

q: Morale among the sailors was very high. “Morale” means:
e: Morale = the mental and emotional condition of a group.

q: The soldiers returned to their barracks after the exercise. “Barracks” are:
e: Barracks = military housing for personnel.

q: He was promoted to a higher rank. A “rank” is:
o: a position in the military hierarchy
e: Rank = official grade (petty officer, commander, major...).

q: The unit will withdraw at dawn. “Withdraw” means:
e: To withdraw = to retreat / move back.

q: Logistics is critical to any campaign. “Logistics” refers to:
o: the supply and movement of troops and equipment
e: Logistics = planning and moving personnel, supplies, and equipment.

q: The patrol was caught in an ambush. An “ambush” is:
o: a surprise attack from a hidden position
e: Ambush = a surprise attack by concealed forces.

q: The colonel issued new orders this morning. “Issued” means:
e: To issue orders = to give them officially.

q: The area is under constant surveillance. “Surveillance” means:
e: Surveillance = continuous watching of a person, place, or activity.

q: He is on leave this week. “Leave” means:
e: Leave = official permission to be absent (vacation).

q: The fleet set sail at dawn. A “fleet” is:
e: Fleet = a large group of ships under one command.

q: The recruits completed basic training. “Recruits” are:
e: Recruit = a person who has recently joined the armed forces.

q: Hostilities ceased at midnight. “Ceased” means:
e: To cease = to stop.

q: They reinforced the position overnight. “Reinforced” means:
o: strengthened with additional troops or material
e: To reinforce = to make stronger with extra forces or support.

q: An NCO briefed the squad. An “NCO” is:
o: a non-commissioned officer, such as a petty officer
e: NCO = Non-Commissioned Officer (corporal, petty officer...).

q: The mission was aborted due to bad weather. “Aborted” means:
e: To abort = to stop an operation before it is finished.

q: The frigate is on patrol in the strait. “Patrol” means:
o: moving through an area to watch and protect it
e: To patrol = to move around an area to monitor or secure it.

q: The convoy reached the port safely. A “convoy” is:
o: a group of vehicles or ships traveling together
e: Convoy = vehicles/ships moving together, often under escort.

q: The officer was court-martialed. “Court-martialed” means:
e: Court-martial = a military trial for offenses against military law.

q: The army mobilized within 48 hours. “Mobilized” means:
o: assembled and prepared forces for action
e: To mobilize = to prepare and organize troops for active service.

q: The crew practiced the fire drill again. A “drill” is:
e: Drill = practice through repetition.

q: The squad took cover behind the wall. “Took cover” means:
e: To take cover = to shelter from enemy fire.

q: They underestimated their adversary. An “adversary” is:
e: Adversary = opponent, enemy.

q: Follow the chain of command. The “chain of command” is:
e: Chain of command = hierarchy through which orders pass.

q: I need to stop for gas before we hit the highway. In American English, “gas” means:
e: Gas = gasoline (petrol in British English).

q: Take the elevator to the fifth floor. An “elevator” is:
o: a machine that carries people between floors
e: Elevator (*US*) = lift (UK).

q: We rented an apartment downtown. “Downtown” means:
e: Downtown = the central business district of a city.

q: He is on vacation until Monday. “Vacation” means:
e: Vacation (*US*) = holiday (UK).

q: Please email me your résumé. A “résumé” is:
o: a summary of your education and work experience
e: Résumé (US) = CV (UK): a summary of your education and work experience.

q: Walk on the sidewalk, not in the street. A “sidewalk” is:
e: Sidewalk (*US*) = pavement (UK).

q: The faucet in the kitchen is leaking. A “faucet” is:
o: a tap that controls water flow
e: Faucet (*US*) = tap (UK).

q: Classes start in the fall. “Fall” means:
e: Fall (*US*) = autumn.

q: My schedule is completely full this week. A “schedule” is:
o: a plan of times for activities
e: Schedule = timetable, planned program.

q: She was really mad at her brother. Here, “mad” means:
e: In American English, mad = angry.

q: I finally figured out the problem with the radio. “Figured out” means:
e: To figure out = to understand or find the solution.

q: Can you give me a ride to the base? A “ride” is:
o: a trip in a vehicle, as a passenger
e: Give someone a ride (*US*) = give someone a lift (UK).

q: The store is two blocks away. A “block” is:
o: a section of street between two intersections
e: Block = the distance between two street corners.

q: He bought candy for the kids. “Candy” means:
e: Candy (*US*) = sweets (UK).

q: The movie starts at eight. A “movie” is:
e: Movie (*US*) = film.

q: Toss it in the trash. “Trash” means:
e: Trash (*US*) = rubbish (UK).

q: I'll call you on my cell. A “cell” here is:
e: Cell (cell phone) = mobile phone.

q: He ordered a burger with french fries. “French fries” are:
e: French fries (*US*) = chips (UK).

q: Would you like a cookie with your coffee? A “cookie” is:
o: a small, flat, sweet baked treat
e: Cookie (US) = biscuit (UK). In American English, a *biscuit* is a small soft bread roll.

q: The restroom is down the hall on the left. A “restroom” is:
e: Restroom (*US*) = public toilet.

q: I bought a round-trip ticket to Washington. “Round-trip” means:
e: Round-trip (*US*) = return ticket (UK).

q: He works the graveyard shift at the harbor. The “graveyard shift” is:
e: Graveyard shift = work period during the night (e.g., midnight–8 a.m.).

q: That new destroyer is awesome! “Awesome” means:
e: Awesome (*US*, informal) = great, excellent.

q: I guess you're right about the schedule. “I guess” means:
e: I guess (*US*) = I suppose.

q: A “sortie” is:
o: a single operational flight by one aircraft
e: Sortie = one operational flight by a single aircraft.

q: “Attrition” refers to:
o: gradual reduction of strength through losses
e: Attrition = the gradual wearing down of forces.

q: A “beachhead” is:
o: a position secured on a hostile shore
e: Beachhead = a position secured on an enemy shore.

q: “Ordnance” means:
e: Ordnance = weapons and ammunition.

q: A “detachment” is:
o: a small unit sent on a separate duty
e: Detachment = a small unit sent away on a separate duty.

q: “Reconnaissance in force” means:
o: an attack made to obtain information
e: Reconnaissance in force = an attack made to find out the enemy's strength and positions.

q: A “contingency plan” is:
o: a plan for a possible future event
e: Contingency plan = a plan ready for a possible future event.

q: “Force projection” means:
o: deploying military power at a distance
e: Force projection = deploying military power far from home.

q: “Deterrence” is:
o: preventing action through fear of consequences
e: Deterrence = preventing action through fear of the consequences.

q: A “task force” is:
o: a temporary grouping for a specific mission
e: Task force = a temporary grouping of units for a specific mission.

q: A “no-fly zone” is:
e: No-fly zone = airspace where flights are prohibited.

q: “Collateral damage” means:
o: unintended harm to civilians or property
e: Collateral damage = unintended harm to civilians or property.

q: “Chain of custody” refers to:
e: Chain of custody: the documented handling of evidence.

q: “Standing orders” are:
e: Standing orders = permanent instructions.

q: A “quartermaster” is responsible for:
e: Quartermaster = the person responsible for supplies and provisions.

q: “Escalation” means:
e: Escalation = an increase in intensity.

q: “Situational awareness” means:
o: understanding what is happening around you
e: Situational awareness = understanding what is happening around you.

q: An “embargo” is:
e: Embargo.

q: “Rules of engagement” determine:
o: when and how force may be used
e: Rules of engagement = rules on when and how force may be used.

q: “Chokepoint” means:
o: a narrow passage that can be blocked
e: Chokepoint = a narrow passage (a strait, a pass, a bridge) that is easy to block.

q: A “briefing” given after an operation is a:
e: Debriefing.

q: “Sustainment” refers to:
o: keeping forces supplied and effective over time
e: Sustainment over time.

q: “To relieve” a unit means:
e: To relieve a unit = to replace it with another unit in its position, so that it can rest or move elsewhere.

q: “Hardware” in a defense context means:
e: Hardware (defense) = military equipment.

q: “Surge capacity” means:
o: the ability to increase output rapidly
e: Surge capacity = the ability to increase output quickly.
